extracted.intended_audience: readers looking for BookTube channels / book lovers seeking channel recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: A directory-style curated list of BookTube (YouTube book community) channels, each entry showing host name, activity date, subscriber count, and a short bio describing content and focus. Intended to help readers discover BookTubers by their niche, tone, and output frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active since
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries include an "Active since [year] -" label (e.g., "Active since 2021 -", "Active since 2016 -", "Active since 2014 -").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates channel longevity and track record; useful for evaluating how established a creator is and how much archived content they may have. No explicit threshold given on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosted by (host name)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries show who hosts the channel using the label "Hosted by [Name]" or similar (e.g., "Hosted by Petrik", "Hosted by Jourdan").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the channel's creator/personality; helps assess perspective, voice, and potential relatability to the viewer. No additional biographical requirements provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscribers (audience size)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subscriber count appears for each channel (e.g., "15,600 Subscribers", "10,900 Subscribers", "29,300 Subscribers").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as a popularity/reach metric for channels; can be used to gauge influence or production scale. The page lists raw counts but provides no interpretation or cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel description / bio (tone & mission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each channel entry includes a short bio or blurb describing the host and their channel (examples: "I'm Petrik. I'm incredibly enthusiastic about novels, manga, anime, video games, music, movies, TV shows, and artworks.", "This channel was inspired by a brown girl dreaming to see herself in ART.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows channel tone, personality, and stated mission; valuable for matching viewer interests (enthusiastic, activist, safe-space, etc.). Use bios to assess whether content aligns with reader tastes; the page provides these verbatim but no evaluation rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content types / video formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Bios list the types of videos the channel produces (examples from page: "book reviews, hauls, and monthly wrap-ups", "wrap-ups, discussion videos, tags", "reviews, hauls, TBR, bookish Endeavors", "reading challenges", "book recommendations").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates format mix (reviews, hauls, wrap-ups, tags, discussion, challenges) important for evaluating whether a channel provides the kinds of videos a viewer wants. The page enumerates formats per channel but does not rank or score them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre / niche focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel blurbs specify genres or topical focus (examples: "romance", "fantasy, science fiction, thriller/horror, hard-hitting contemporary, mangas and graphic novels", "books that centre African-descended peoples", "Romance Booktuber").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to filter channels by subject matter or demographic focus (age levels: middle grade, YA, adult; genres: fantasy, romance, horror; identity-focused content). The directory records these specializations but gives no selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload schedule / frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Some entries state posting frequency or schedule (examples: "Videos released on Tuesday and Thursday, occasionally more days!!", "I upload videos every Monday, Wednesday, & Friday!", "I make videos every week").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency/frequency metric for assessing active engagement and expected new content cadence. The page contains schedule statements when channels provide them; no standard for 'good' frequency is offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community positioning / audience identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Bios sometimes include statements about community stance or intended audience (examples: "This channel discusses all things Entertainment; mainly featuring the works of minorities, primarily black women.", "I am a queer, multiracial, girl...", "this is a safe space!", "reading and writing is political and empowering").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals whether a channel targets specific identity groups or promotes particular community values; useful for viewers seeking inclusive/safe or politically engaged book content. The page reproduces these statements but does not evaluate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of coverage and focus breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries indicate breadth of reading coverage (examples: "I will read mostly anything so here you’ll find all kinds of reader content", "I read a wide range of genres and age types (middle grade, young adult, and adult)").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows whether a channel is generalist or specialist; helps viewers looking for broad recommendations versus focused expertise. The listing shows these traits per channel without standardized categorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curation transparency (selection criteria not stated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Page title: "A Curated List of 100+ BookTubers" but the list provides no explicit explanation of the selection or inclusion criteria for channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of stated curation criteria means readers cannot know the standards used to include channels (e.g., quality, diversity, subscriber minimums). For evaluative use, one must infer importance from listed metadata (bio, subscribers, longevity) because the curator's selection rubric is not provided.
